import pandas as pd

# Load source tables
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_56/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_56/training_1.csv"

# Read CSVs with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN on "city"
# Both tables have a "city" column, join on this column
joined_df = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="city", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by on Source2_56_0.city and aggregation sum(Source2_56_0.fare)
# After join, the fare column from Source2_56_0 is "fare" (no suffix added because only df0 has it)
# Group by city and sum fare
grouped_df = joined_df.groupby("city", as_index=False)["fare"].sum()

# Ensure the schema matches target schema: ['city': string, 'fare': float]
# Convert city to string and fare to float explicitly
grouped_df["city"] = grouped_df["city"].astype(str)
grouped_df["fare"] = grouped_df["fare"].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_56/target_multisource.csv"
grouped_df.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
